findings.title: The GM's give and take windows are drawn once: only the hub's holdings follow the world; the counts, the key list, the Remnant list and the Take list stay as opened
findings.surface: Give / take items; Give an item; Give a Truth Bullet; Take an item away; Issue an Autopsy
findings.control: the category selects' carry counts; Which key; Remnant; Which item; the Autopsy's boxes
findings.where: scripts/gm-items.mjs:149-155 (the one keepLive), 371-381 (the Give tab's lists read once), 1018-1019, 1482, 1763-1800, 1632-1656
findings.what_happens: openItemManager keeps one region live, .drpg-holdings-live, on item and actor hooks. The Give tab under it is built once from what the world held at the open: giveCategoryOptions' 'Gear 1/3' counts in both category selects, keyChoices' bedrooms not held, bulletTraces' Remnants on every scene. A change of the student select rebuilds them; nothing else does. The same holds for the standalone windows: Give an item's counts, Give a Truth Bullet's trace list, Take's item list, and the Autopsy's dead marks and planned fill. A player who picks up, stows or hands over a thing, a Remnant placed or erased by another GM, or a key handed over by a student, leaves the lists as they were until the window is reopened.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM with Give / take open on Anna watches the holdings line go to 'Gear: 3/3' after Anna finds a tool, while the Give tab's category select under it still reads 'Cleaning Tool (Gear 2/3)' and the key select still offers the key Bob just handed her.
findings.expected: the Give tab's counts, key list and Remnant list redrawn on the same sources as the holdings (items, actors, Remnant tokens, region flags), keeping the picked values; the standalone windows the same or at least their lists
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a second keepLive or keepFresh in gm-items.mjs: one call (149). wireGiveForm's recipient listener (798-809) and showKeyChoices (313) run only on the select's change. bulletTraces is called at 372 and 1482 only. The holdings region is the comment's stated scope (121-138, 'the number it shows is the one the GM is about to act on'), which the Give tab's counts repeat. The give is checked again where it matters: an over-cap item is given on purpose (override true), a trace gone is warned (1319-1321), a bullet already held is said (1589-1592); a key already held is not (finding 2). No test drives a change under an open hub (R4060 reads the footer).

findings.title: The Level Up button's 'on offer' mark on a GM's sheet does not follow the GMs' offers: no listener on the store, and the primary draws nothing for an offer another GM made
findings.what_happens: On a GM's sheet the button reads standingOffers, the GMs' store offerStore. Its setting gmOffers is a client setting with no onChange, and the store row has no change hook, so a merge from another GM draws no sheet. The redraws that exist are local: dropOffer renders the primary's own sheet after a spend (274), takeBackOffer and offerAdvancement render the acting GM's own (444, 517). recordOffer, which the primary runs for an offer a second GM asked for, renders nothing. So the primary's open sheet shows no offer a second GM made, and a second GM's open sheet keeps 'is-offered' and '1 Level Up on offer' after the player spent it. The tooltip and the class are all that is stale; the press reads the store afresh.

The setting's onChange only toggles the body class drpg-resources-locked, whose rules (danganronpa.css:1504-1517, 5886-5888) dim Hope, the Party sheet's toggles and the trait inputs, not .drpg-reserve-field; the setting is not in sync.mjs SETTING_KINDS. A GM turning the lock on leaves an open player's sheet with a live field (a write then judged and put back by the GMs); turning it off leaves the read-only number until the sheet renders.
findings.failure_scenario: The GM locks player resources mid-session; a player whose sheet is open still sees Health as a field, types 3, and watches it snap back with a refusal.
findings.expected: the open sheets redrawn when the setting changes (refreshSheets in its onChange)
findings.refutation_tried: grep drpg-reserve-field in styles: only its look (danganronpa.css:9081-9098). writeReserve (389-395) does not ask the lock itself; resource-guard.mjs and the GMs' audit judge the write (the trust model's 'courtesy'), so the rule holds and only the screen lies.
findings.probe: player's sheet open with Lock off; GM sets lockPlayerResources true; read the player's .drpg-reserve-field (still there)

findings.title: The sheet's room-bound parts are drawn at the render and nothing redraws them for another character's move, a room's flags or a stash elsewhere
findings.surface: Character sheet - the Actions tab; the Inventory tab; the sidebar
findings.control: action tiles' room reasons; Rifle and the open stash section; the own stash sections; the lair's Lock line
findings.what_happens: roomBlockFor dims Search, Observe, Listen, Palm, Tamper and Facilities by where the character stands and who else is there (locateActor, othersInRoom, neighbouringRooms, facilitiesShutReason); the Inventory draws Rifle only while somebody else's open stash with things in it stands in the room (openStashesHere) and the own stash sections from the scene's stash flags; the lair line reads the room's lock flag. Of sheet.mjs's hooks none hears a token or a region: a sheet renders on its own actor's and items' updates and on refreshSheets. So another student walking in or out (Palm's 'nobody here', Tamper's witnesses), another student stashing a thing or a stash set up, concealed or found, a room lock or a facility flag changed, and a move that writes nothing to the actor leave these parts as drawn. forgetTamper clears the ledger cache on remnantSecrets and paints nothing. The module calls the dimming advice and judges every press again (the note above roomBlockFor, 955-960), so the presses are safe; what is shown is not.
findings.evidence:
* Deliberately NOT a hard block: the tile stays clickable ...
* guards downstream stay exactly where they are, since a room's state can

[sheet-sidebar.mjs:668-672]

findings.failure_scenario: Kaede stands alone in the kitchen with her sheet open, Palm struck through 'Nobody else is here'; Hiro walks in and the tile stays struck through until something else renders her sheet.
findings.expected: the open sheets of the characters in a room redrawn (or their room parts repainted) on a token's room change, a region's flags and a stash's items, as the HUD is
findings.refutation_tried: With Move charging on (settings.mjs:3203-3210, default true) a character's own crossing writes its purse and so renders its own sheet; the gap is the other sources. sync.mjs KIND_REFRESH runs 'sheets' for the clock, the Eclipse, visibility, projects, search tokens, restrictions, the incident, rules and overflow, none of them a token's room or a region's stash flags. passages-gm.mjs's updateRegion hooks redraw the GMs' overlay only. The comments call the room reasons advice (by decision) but the owner's rule of 20.11.2026 asks the window to show the change.
